note: Families group the engine's generators, recipes and GLSL modules by what they do in a composition. `python scripts/families.py check` proves the manifest matches the engine. Cost classes come from `node scripts/layer_cost.mjs --write` (ms per frame above an empty frame, 1920x1080 at half resolution, software rendering on the author's machine; low < 8, medium < 20, high >= 20). Items that need media, run your own code or are not a layer say `unmeasured`. Absolute numbers depend on the machine, the order does not. Everything here is the project's own code; ideas from other projects are concepts only (repo-analysis.md).

families.ground: the quiet matter everything else is read against
families.figure: the single dominant thing a composition is about
families.structure: grid, rhythm and texture that measure the figure
families.information: type, instruments and data: what the viewer reads
families.finish: the last pass: vignette, scanlines, dither, LED emulation
families.form: GLSL distance fields, raymarching and spatial helpers
families.colour: GLSL colour spaces and tone mapping

bg.note: The quiet reference; grain only on screens, never on LED.

shader.role: GLSL field: slow matter or a hero field
shader.note: Every shader reads the audio bus; keep fills low when it is a ground.

sim.role: reaction-diffusion or ink, baked in a loop
sim.note: The first frame bakes the loop (about 1.4 s measured in headless software rendering; cached after that); raise `threshold` so it leaves empty space.

flow.note: Needs width of 2 or more to survive distance.

organism.role: point-cloud form with spin and breath
organism.note: Dot of 2 or more; fine dust vanishes at distance.

tunnel.note: The default hero for a wall; heavy stroke on LED.

shape.note: The cleanest way to make one dominant figure.

lines.note: Cover under 10% of the frame as a hero, or nothing is left to breathe.

logo.role: white mask of a supplied logo

model.note: Rasterised on canvas 2D; shader, wireframe or points.

splat.note: Isotropic approximation; keep under 15000 points live.

parallax.note: The model-based depth path was never tested here; a depth map you supply is fine.

structure.note: The measure the eye reads the hero against.

bitfield.note: Fills about half the frame by nature: use at 10-20% opacity as texture, never as the hero.

measure.note: Reads as data, not as image.

instrument.role: spectrum, scope, radar, rings tied to the real signal
instrument.note: Cause and effect: shows what drives the picture.

data.note: Small, calm, always in the same place.

hud.note: Tells the viewer the system is alive.

text.note: Prefer `typeset` when there is more than one level.

typeset.role: title, caption and data as one hierarchy; reveal by glyph or word; text on a path
typeset.note: Hidden at both ends of the loop, so it closes.

code.role: custom drawing code with the kit K
code.note: Not a sandbox: lint plus per-project authorisation.

fx.role: one-pass effect that reads everything below it: CRT, VHS, halftone, dither, edges, glass, bloom, glitch, tiling
fx.note: Order matters: it only sees the layers underneath. Keep one or two per composition; on LED prefer PAINEL DE LED, DITHER and GRADE, avoid CRT and VHS.

synth.role: one-line chain (osc, noise, voronoi, shape… then kaleid, modulate, tint…) compiled to a shader
synth.note: Write the chain, not the GLSL. Cycles are whole numbers per loop so the loop closes; numbers accept bass, hit, p1..p4.

isf.role: one of 84 ready ISF generators chosen in the layer parameters (lib); p1..p4 drive its first four float inputs
isf.note: The shader is picked, not written: use it as a ground or accent when a ready generator fits the concept. Credit and licence of each shader are in isf-library/README.md.

blobs.role: detect and mark blobs in the image below (by brightness, contrast, colour or luminance zone): boxes, ids, links
blobs.note: Reads the stack below it like fx. Stateless: ids follow area order, not identity over time.
